sources.name: Canadian Protected and Conserved Areas Database (CPCAD), ECCC
sources.resolution: Polygon boundaries generalised by the server to about 0.0004 degree (30-45 m)
sources.note: 5 protected or conserved areas intersect the study box. Absence here does not clear provincial wildlife, wetland or Crown-land rules.

sources.name: CanVec 1:50 000 Resource Management (power_line_1, transformer_station_0/2), NRCan
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - Canada. Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada
sources.resolution: 1:50 000 topographic base map (stated horizontal accuracy in haccmin/haccmax, typically 10-20 m)
sources.note: 17 mapped power lines and 3 transformer stations within 30 km. Feature source dates (datemin/datemax) are shown per candidate; many are decades old. No voltage, owner or available capacity is attributed. This is mapped infrastructure, not a confirmed interconnection point.

sources.name: Global Solar Atlas 2.0 long-term averages (Solargis model), point API
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0. Global Solar Atlas 2.0, a free, web-based application developed and operated by Solargis s.r.o. on behalf of the World Bank Group, utilizing Solargis data, with funding provided by ESMAP
sources.resolution: Modelled grid, about 9 arcseconds (~250 m) for GHI; one value at each solar candidate centroid
sources.note: PVOUT_csi is Solargis modelled yield for a crystalline-silicon, ground-mounted, optimally tilted system with typical losses. It is a long-term average, not a guarantee.
